All I could smell was vinegar. It was everywhere. Splattered over the walls, the broken counters, eating into the bodies on the floor.

Yep. Bodies, plural. This had been a big one. They didn't usually make it this far uptown before being caught and dispatched, but it was bound to happen sooner or later.

Shit. I was used to dealing with poltergeists, ghouls, and the occasional zombie shuffling around an office trying to finish their paperwork. Just little trifles, trying to hang on to whatever vestiges of life they could. Nothing serious, like this.

Coughing from the overpowering smell, I stumbled forward and grabbed a railing to secure myself. My hand came away wet and sticky, I could feel the acids and poison scratching at my palm. I grimaced and wiped it down the side of my new sport coat. What a night, I thought to myself, as I continued forward into the not very metaphorical slaughterhouse.

The farther I crept, the more the hair on my neck began to rise. I could feel the energy of the city disappearing behind me, as if there was a veil draped over the doorway. That wasn't a good sign, it meant it had reclaimed this land and I could bet it intended to defend itself.

Why couldn't we just talk, for once? We've been fighting each other for thousands of years, you would think somebody would have learned the language.

A sharp rattling interrupted my thoughts, and I swiveled my head to locate it's source. It was coming from the room at the end of the darkened hall. Of course it was, I thought, as I put my back against the wall and slowly slid down to the grime covered linoleum floor.

I could feel the barest pulse of electricity coming from the wiring underneath the house, as I squatted against the wall. Putting my hand amongst the filth, I tried to concentrate on pulling as much as I could while I stared unblinkingly at the end of the hallway. The darkness was utterly complete, and that was far from reassuring.

I finally felt the wire go dead under my hand as a loud sigh wound its way through the open windows of the house. The wind was grating, in that dead silence, and it felt like I was in the mouth of some great creature, listening to its breath. The house creaked along with the wind and fell silent once again.

Muttering internal obscenities about my choice of profession, I inched forward and grasped the doorknob. It clicked and creaked as I turned it and pushed the door open from the side. When nothing tried to kill me after a few seconds, I cautiously peered around the corner into the room.

It was massive. Twelve feet tall, and half as wide, Its rough brown skin was stretched and broken around its frame. You could see the past battles it had survived, in its skin. It was old. Much older than the ones around these days. I could see two figures at its base, being slowly enveloped by its tendrils.

I should have already been dead, I knew, saved by the fact it was more focused on feeding than it was looking out for a lone Watchman.

Fuck fuck fuuuuck, this was a mistake. I should have waited for the others, I opined in my head as I stared at the creature's back. Maybe I can back out before it senses me, I fervently wished, as I moved to slowly walk backward down the hall.

Of course I didn't make it two steps before my the hallway creaked under my foot. I hurriedly cast a glance at the door, thinking maybe it hadn't -

A crash and roar, as the wall bowed out and the hallway filled with hundreds of green capped limbs reaching for me. I didn't take another step before they wrapped around my body and started to squeeze. I could feel its limbs wrap around every available inch and hold me in the air while the breath was forced from my body. I only had seconds left, I could already feel my mind getting sluggish.

There was nothing I could do. I was too far away from the city, too far away from the power I needed to save me. A fucking city watchman, killed because they cut the power. You've got to be kidding me. They'll bring me back just to kill me again for being a failure.

I can feel the limbs loosen just enough for me to retain consciousness, as it dragged me back into the room. It held me up in front of its trunk as if to look at me. They don't have eyes, we know, but we're not sure exactly how they sense us. This one was fucking looking at me, though, I could feel it in my bones.

It let out another gust of air and shook it's buds at me as I felt its limbs tighten again and pull at my extremities. It wasn't satisfied to just kill me, it was going to fucking dismember me. I could feel my joints pop out as I let out scream after scream. My throat was tearing from the effort, and I could taste the blood in my mouth mixing with my spittle. Just as I started to slide very ungracefully into shock, I caught a glimpse of light through a crack in the wall. There was a live wire right there, all I had to was concentrate --

Like it could hear me, it redoubled its efforts to tear me apart. I could hear my bones crushing as it pulled tighter, trying to snuff my light even as I reached across the void. My vision was starting to close in, as I felt that familiar tickle in my head. I didn't have enough time to do this right. I opened the floodgates and felt the power arc through me as I lost focus and died.

But only for a little bit. Watchman are hard to kill, by design, and I told you they'd bring me back anyway. It was Korin who did it, that son of a bitch. I know he's going to lord this over me for years.

Nobody talked, as I was picked up and carted to the door. McLoughten put his hand on my shoulder and I gasped in renewed pain. Shit, I didn't think I'd ever be happy to feel pain. I tried to look up at him, but I was half blind from all the broken blood vessels in my eyes. He was pointing to the corner, and my eyes eventually followed his hand. He was pointing at what was left of the creature. Its limbs were twisted in agony, and it was smoking as blue tendrils of light danced on what was left.

"Sequoia sempervirens", McLoughten muttered, as his hand absentmindedly traced its outline. "You should have fucking died, man. Died for real. You're luckier than a goddamn rabbit's foot. The slippage alone... You must have pulled 200,000 volts. Everything in a half mile is fried. That's how we found you. You blew every transformer from here to Gotter Plaza."

"Yeah," I rasped. "I figured I'd make you assholes do a little work, if I was going out."

There were appreciative chuckles as McLoughten took his hand from my shoulder.

"Hurry up and heal, Nygaard," He intoned."The Midnight Mayor is going to meet you at the hospital. It's not often a thrice year survives something like this, and I'm sure he's going to want a full recollection of what happened."

I'm sure my face lost what little colour it had left, at those words. The Midnight fucking Mayor, Matthew Swift himself.
